$comment: What a reader of the checks ruled (scripts/assessments/reviews/). drop: lessons of a unit whose section is not in the check, with the reason. instruction: the direction line of a worksheet type when its cards stand in a check (the worksheet's own line is written for a whole page). noCheck: units that get no check, with the reason. blend: a worksheet type whose part also takes boxes from other types of the same lesson and shape, in turn. sameGiven: types whose form B box prints the numbers form A prints (the same fraction of another group). lowestTerms: types whose answer is a fraction that must not have a second right answer in smaller numbers. avoidAns: per type a pattern no answer of a box may match. pairKind: types of two fractions, taken only when they share the top or the bottom number, form B like form A. sameLook: types without numbers whose form B box has about as much drawing as form A (the same number of parts).

k-sorting-tallies-days.4: [en.review-k1-math] Which of two things is heavier has no sure answer for the pairs the generator draws (apple or pear; camel or panda).

k-putting-together-number-bonds.4: [en.review-k1-math] The missing part of 20 without a picture cannot be tried by a child before the unit; far above the bonds of 5 in the part before it.

g2-place-value-to-1000.1: [en.review-g23-math] The answer frame of the worksheet reads "[ ] ■×10 + [ ]": a second grader has not met the multiplication sign, and nothing says which box is tens and which is ones.

instruction.K-016: The pictures are in pairs. If one is left over, the number is odd. Circle odd or even.
instruction.G1-287: Each card shows a double. Write how many in all.
instruction.G2-305: This number line does not start at 0. Write the number each arrow points to.
instruction.G2-210: Count the equal groups. Finish the multiplication sentence. Write how many in all.
instruction.G2-233: Look at the fraction. Circle that part of the group. Write how many you circled.
instruction.G3-320: Look at the fraction. Circle that part of the group. Write how many you circled.
instruction.G3-338: Look at the first rectangle. Circle the rectangle on the right that covers the SAME number of squares.
instruction.G3-337: Count the sides of the small squares all the way around each rectangle. Write the perimeter.
instruction.G3-339: Look at the first rectangle. Circle the rectangle on the right with the SAME distance around.
instruction.G3-346: Count all the cubes in each shape. Write the total.
instruction.G3-321: The small square is one part of a whole. Read its fraction. Circle the bar that shows the WHOLE.
instruction.G3-319: Look at both bars. Circle the greater fraction.

noCheck.g2-shapes-solids-symmetry: [en.review-g23-math] The pictures keyed as symmetrical are drawn with shading and uneven details (a persimmon with a highlight on one side, a bat with a mouth mark left of the line): "no" can be defended. Without that part the unit has two parts, fewer than a check needs.
noCheck.g3-time-temperature-mass-volume: [en.review-g23-math] The clocks offer a choice one minute from the key while the minute hand stops short of the minute marks; 24-hour time is not taught in U.S. Grades K-3. One part would be left.

reasons.K-016 avoid 10: [en.review-k1-math-2] With 10 pictures the fifth pair stands alone under the row, where the leftover picture stands in the other boxes: a child can read it as one left over.
reasons.K-032 instruction: The worksheet says "in each row"; a check has one row.
reasons.G3-364 blend G3-365: The lesson is the facts of 2 and of 5 and hands out one worksheet per table; a part cut from the first alone asks no fact of 5.
reasons.instructions of 2026-11-12: [en.review-g23-math] Ten direction lines reworded for a box that stands alone and for U.S. classrooms (what to write, which rectangle to compare with, "greater" for numbers, "shape" for a wall of cubes).
reasons.G2-233 G3-320 sameGiven: [en.review-g23-math] A half of a group in form A and a fourth in form B are not one level.
reasons.G3-315 lowestTerms: [en.review-g23-math] 2 of 4 shaded is 2/4 and 1/2: both are right, and the unit teaches exactly that.
reasons.G3-317 avoidAns: [en.review-g23-math] The first mark after 0 (a unit fraction) is the easiest point of a number line; both forms mark a fraction with a top number above 1.
reasons.G3-319 pairKind: [en.review-g23-math] Grade 3 compares fractions with the same top or the same bottom number; 1/3 against 4/6 is another task.
reasons.G3-343 sameLook: [en.review-g23-math] Shapes cut into eight parts in form A and two halves in form B are not one level.
reasons.one number once per form: [en.review-g23-math] In a check on counting to 10 the number 5 was the answer three times in one form.
reasons.three-digit numbers: [en.review-g23-math] 262 reads the same with its places in the wrong order; all four pairs to compare were decided by the hundreds alone.
